title: How a Heat Pump Works in 60 Seconds ♨️❄️ #shorts
description:
A heat pump doesn't make heat, it moves it. Refrigerant soaks up warmth from cold outdoor air, a compressor squeezes it until it's hot, and an indoor coil releases that heat into your home. Flip a valve and the same machine cools your house in summer. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#heatpump #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A heat pump can deliver *3 to 4 times* more heat than the electricity it uses.

steps.label: Outdoor coil
steps.text: Outside, very cold *refrigerant* soaks up heat, even from chilly winter air.

steps.label: Compressor
steps.text: A *compressor* squeezes that gas, and squeezing makes it much *hotter*.

steps.label: Indoor coil
steps.text: The hot gas flows indoors, and a fan blows air across the coil to *warm your home*.

steps.label: Expansion
steps.text: Then an *expansion valve* drops the pressure, so the refrigerant turns icy cold again.

steps.label: Reverse
steps.text: In summer, a *reversing valve* flips the flow, and it pumps heat *out* instead.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Absorb, squeeze, *release*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
